features.title: GetMCP 1.8.0 migration and guarded compatibility
features.intent: Preserve existing server settings, credentials, grants and access while migrating reviewed legacy records; keep unsupported paths guarded.

provenance.description: Preserve existing settings, credentials and access during an upgrade; retain the guard for unsupported dependencies.

scenarios.title: Review and migrate an eligible empty sign-in server

inputs.fixture: isolated synthetic server without tools, custom settings, grants or gateway dependencies

scenarios.reason: Local database and synthetic OAuth HTTP checks are separate from a Studio browser execution.
scenarios.recovery: Bind an owned disposable 1.8.0 fixture, review and migrate the synthetic server in the admin interface, and verify the independently stored row and access.

scenarios.title: Refuse dependent or unauthorized migration

inputs.fixture: synthetic server with a tool, grant or gateway dependency

scenarios.reason: Local direct and REST refusal checks exist; no Studio browser and independent state binding is recorded.
scenarios.recovery: Bind the protected fixture and denied role in Studio, submit the direct request, and compare the persisted server and credential state.

scenarios.title: Automatically migrate reviewed legacy servers and retain grants

inputs.fixture: owned 1.7 snapshot with a standard server, gateway, remote server and synthetic grants

scenarios.reason: The actual reviewed compatibility profile passed local HTTP rehearsal; Studio and real-provider acceptance are incomplete.
scenarios.recovery: Bind an isolated supported fixture and verify automatic upgrade, real client authorization, saved records and rollback.

scenarios.title: Refuse conflicting upstream grant stores

inputs.fixture: owned legacy grant and conflicting synthetic destination

scenarios.reason: Local database conflict and retry tests passed; no Studio fixture is bound.
scenarios.recovery: Bind a disposable fixture, introduce a conflicting grant store and independently compare both records after refusal.

scenarios.title: Recover an already-upgraded native grant table

inputs.fixture: owned old-primary-key table with separated legacy and native synthetic grants

scenarios.reason: Local schema and already-upgraded HTTP rehearsals passed; no Studio fixture is bound.
scenarios.recovery: Bind a disposable mixed-store fixture and independently verify both grants, the native key and repeated activation.

scenarios.title: Leave unknown or referenced grant-table schemas unchanged

inputs.fixture: owned synthetic grant table with an unreviewed column or foreign-key reference

scenarios.reason: Local refusal checks passed; no Studio fixture is bound.
scenarios.recovery: Bind a disposable fixture and independently compare the table definition and grant rows after refusal.

scenarios.title: Identify legacy servers deferred from automatic migration

inputs.fixture: owned legacy server with an unreviewed setting

scenarios.reason: Local WordPress refusal and notice checks passed; no Studio fixture is bound.
scenarios.recovery: Bind a disposable deferred server and verify its escaped name, ID and status, administrator-only notice, stored settings, authorization and automatic retry.

scenarios.title: Flag a Gateway whose prior delegation cannot be verified

inputs.fixture: owned already-upgraded Gateway without a pre-upgrade snapshot

scenarios.reason: Local WordPress review and authorization checks passed; no Studio fixture is bound.
scenarios.recovery: Bind a disposable Gateway without history and verify affected member names and IDs, the direct Gateway link, administrator-only warning and unchanged member access.

scenarios.title: Preserve proven Gateway members at the old 500-server boundary

inputs.fixture: owned synthetic Gateway with more than 500 active servers and names tied across the boundary

scenarios.reason: Local synthetic database checks passed; no Studio fixture is bound.
scenarios.recovery: Bind a disposable large Gateway, verify known members and independently confirm tied boundary members were not guessed.

scenarios.title: Show inherited project gateway capabilities as ready

inputs.fixture: active legacy gateway with one active native member and an enabled tool

scenarios.reason: Local WordPress readiness and inherited tool checks passed; no Studio browser fixture is bound.
scenarios.recovery: Bind a disposable gateway and verify its readiness badge and inherited capability independently.

scenarios.title: Keep unavailable gateways and invalid remotes not ready

inputs.fixture: paused gateway, inactive member and remote with invalid URL

scenarios.reason: Local WordPress refusal and anonymous-access checks passed; no Studio browser fixture is bound.
scenarios.recovery: Bind disposable unavailable gateways and verify readiness and access remain restricted.

scenarios.title: Preserve gateway delegation without widening direct access

inputs.fixture: gateway user, denied user, remote member and synthetic personal grant

scenarios.reason: Local HTTP and isolated router checks passed; Studio and real-provider acceptance remain open.
scenarios.recovery: Use separate fixture users and a disposable upstream to verify delegation, direct denial, scope and immediate revocation.

scenarios.title: Keep legacy and native OAuth client metadata routes separate

inputs.fixture: one legacy remote and one native 1.8 remote

scenarios.reason: Local REST checks passed; public HTTPS/provider discovery is not verified.
scenarios.recovery: Bind disposable legacy and native OAuth servers and verify metadata discovery from an authorized provider.

scenarios.title: Publish an eligible personal provider grant through the account Gateway

inputs.fixture: two disposable users with isolated synthetic OAuth grants
inputs.expected: only the authenticated user personal grant and reviewed provider endpoints

scenarios.reason: Synthetic local protocol tests pass; external OAuth provider and public HTTPS verification remain pending.
scenarios.recovery: Connect a disposable provider account and exercise the public Gateway.

scenarios.title: Refuse another user or an unreviewed personal provider endpoint

inputs.fixture: two disposable users with isolated synthetic OAuth grants
inputs.expected: only the authenticated user personal grant and reviewed provider endpoints

scenarios.reason: Synthetic local protocol tests pass; external OAuth provider and public HTTPS verification remain pending.
scenarios.recovery: Connect a disposable provider account and exercise the public Gateway.

scenarios.title: Migrate existing native and mailbox servers with supported execution timeouts

inputs.fixture: disposable HTTP and mailbox servers with encrypted test credentials and a bounded timeout
inputs.expected: automatic migration while preserving settings, credentials and access

scenarios.reason: Synthetic local migration tests pass; browser-based upgrade verification remains pending.
scenarios.recovery: Run a disposable 1.7 to 1.8 upgrade through the admin UI.

scenarios.title: Keep Oura authorization and rotation bound to each user

inputs.fixture: Two eligible users and synthetic Oura tokens with single-use refresh

scenarios.reason: Disposable WordPress runtime checks passed locally; Studio browser execution and real-provider acceptance are not established.
scenarios.recovery: Connect separately, call through a Gateway, rotate a token and confirm independent encrypted grants.

scenarios.title: Refuse cross-user Oura access and omit health payloads from logs

inputs.fixture: Two users with distinct health responses, an invalid endpoint and an interrupted refresh

scenarios.reason: Disposable WordPress runtime checks passed locally; Studio browser execution and real-provider acceptance are not established.
scenarios.recovery: Exercise direct denied calls and inspect caches, logs, hooks and saved token state.

scenarios.title: Restore only explicitly granted public read-only Gateway access

inputs.fixture: An opted-in public origin, one granted and one ungranted user, and an active project gateway

scenarios.reason: Disposable WordPress runtime checks passed locally; Studio browser execution and real-provider acceptance are not established.
scenarios.recovery: Verify both gateway routes, stripped credentials, revocation, and refusal after an endpoint or method change.

features.title: Official hosted MCP catalogue
features.intent: Browse hosted MCP servers separately from Templates, save and authorize with the creator selected, and use explicit project gateways without creating native tools.

provenance.description: Owner requested hosted official templates from the supplied catalogues through the gateway module.

scenarios.title: Search, save and authorize with creator-only access and responsive layout
scenarios.reason: Separate local browser and editor tests cover responsive layout and the save/authorize contract. No immutable Studio fixture bindings or execution receipt exist.
scenarios.recovery: Bind an owned disposable GetMCP fixture and catalogue selectors in Studio, execute search, draft save and reload, and retain the result receipt.

scenarios.title: Keep gateway connections and remote catalogue on distinct routes

inputs.fixtures: owned draft gateway and remote connection without credentials

scenarios.reason: Local browser navigation and adapter contracts passed; no bound Studio receipt exists.
scenarios.recovery: Bind disposable records in Studio, click both native and WordPress menus, verify list contents and highlights, reload both routes and use Back/Forward.

scenarios.title: Deny unauthorized catalogue access and revoke upstream access on gateway removal
scenarios.reason: Local WordPress integration covers these refusals, but Studio has no bound multi-user and gateway fixture for the scenario.
scenarios.recovery: Bind isolated users and gateway membership in Studio; verify refusal before membership, authorized delegation and immediate refusal after removal.

scenarios.title: Verify an individual provider's personal OAuth, discovery and harmless read
scenarios.reason: No real provider consent, account changes or exhaustive live compatibility tests were authorized or executed for this catalogue feature.
scenarios.recovery: Obtain a named provider acceptance scope, bind isolated test accounts, and verify consent, refresh, discovery and harmless read separately for that provider.

features.title: Google Health personal reads and summaries
features.intent: Install native read tools with personal Google OAuth and privacy-safe daily/weekly summaries, including available nutrition data; preserve unrelated fixture state.

provenance.description: Owner authorized native Google Health reads, summaries, available nutrition and local shared-fixture tests.

scenarios.title: Install read tools and read daily/weekly summaries with available nutrition
scenarios.reason: Local synthetic-provider integration checks exist. Studio template-install, personal-consent and MCP tool bindings have not been imported/reviewed.
scenarios.recovery: Import the current immutable plugin snapshot into Studio, inspect supported recipes and bindings, review the preview, then run the bound owned-fixture scenarios and retain execution receipts.

scenarios.title: Refuse missing nutrition scope, removed user and disconnected grant
scenarios.reason: Local direct executor refusals exist. No Studio recipe binds OAuth grant changes and denied MCP calls to an independent persisted-state oracle.
scenarios.recovery: Import the current immutable plugin snapshot into Studio, inspect supported recipes and bindings, review the preview, then run the bound owned-fixture scenarios and retain execution receipts.

scenarios.title: Filter nested identity/location fields and retain no health payload in logs/cache
scenarios.reason: Real protocol/database assertions exist locally. Studio database/cache assertions and browser log drawer bindings are unavailable.
scenarios.recovery: Import the current immutable plugin snapshot into Studio, inspect supported recipes and bindings, review the preview, then run the bound owned-fixture scenarios and retain execution receipts.
